newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Assembly session would be sterile - Israeli envoy.
newsitem.headline: Assembly session would be sterile - Israeli envoy.

text.p: Israeli U.N. envoy David Peleg said on Wednesday an emergency special session of the General Assembly requested by Arab states on the issue of Israeli settlements would only prove sterile and be a source of further polarisation.
"Only direct negotiations between the sides can bring about reconciliation," Peleg told reporters.

Noting the issue had been debated twice last month by the Security Council and once by the Assembly, he said: "We definitely feel that another session can only prove sterile ... it would become a source of further polarisation."

He said recent Arab initiatives, including calls by a foreign ministers' meeting in Cairo for a freeze in relations with Israel and a resumption of the Arab economic boycott, seemed intended to "turn the clock back and bring the area back to the era before the Madrid peace conference" that launched the peace process in 1991.

The 22-member Arab group has asked for the emergency special Assembly session under a 1950 "uniting for peace" formula, after the United States twice vetoed Security Council resolutions calling on Israel to halt the building of 6,500 homes for Jews on land captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The site, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, is called Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic and Har Homa in Hebrew.

Peleg said he hoped that when Secretary-General Kofi Annan canvassed all 185 U.N. members about convening the session, which requires the backing of a majority, they would "send the message that the solution to the outstanding issues between the Arabs and Israel will come through direct negotiations in the area and not through resolutions in the United Nations."

Israel was "committed 100 percent to the peace process," he said. It was vital for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and the Palestinian Authority "to take clear steps against terrorism to enable the resumption of the talks between us and the Palestinians on all levels, including the level of Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu and Chairman Arafat."

He was referring to the March 21 suicide bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe in which three Israelis were killed and many were wounded, the bombing of a bus on Wednesday that wounded 11 Israeli soldiers and other recent violent incidents.

Asked about reports the Palestinian Authority had arrested 30 members of the Islamic Jihad group after what Israel said were two botched suicide bombings aimed at Israeli school buses in the Gaza Strip, Peleg said this was "an important step, in the same way that the (recent) release of Hamas terrorists ... was a very negative sign."
